Moral responsibility cannot be adequately grounded in a framework that reduces human action to causal-mechanical processes, for such a reduction erodes the foundational elements of agency that responsibility attributions demand. Ascriptions of moral responsibility presuppose that agents could have done otherwise, embodying a counterfactual competence condition that deterministic causal chains cannot satisfy without importing a normative surplus the mechanistic framework does not contain, as the chains describe only what did occur rather than what ought to have been possible in a sense that carries evaluative weight.
